solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Displaying deplorable timidity in fashion knowledge (7)

blocks.note: ken = range of knowledge, as in 'beyond my ken'

annotation.surface: Someone scorned for being too timid to show off what they know about fashion.
annotation.walkthrough: "In fashion" looks like a container instruction, but it is a single synonym: CHIC.
annotation.definitionFit: To be chicken is to be cowardly, which is a deplorable timidity on display.

entries.clue: Hollywood A-lister just entertains cruciverbalists, one hoping for big hits? (13)

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to hold them inside, so RIGHT holds WE

blocks.note: cruciverbalists are crossword solvers, i.e. we who are reading this

annotation.surface: A film star generously hosting a gathering of crossword fans.
annotation.walkthrough: The setter addresses the solvers directly: cruciverbalists are us, so WE. The question mark flags that "big hits" are punches, not box-office successes.
annotation.definitionFit: A cruiserweight is a boxer in a heavy weight division, who hopes to land big punches.

entries.clue: Temporary buzz word plugged by newspaper (7)

indicators.note: a hole plugged by something has that thing stuffed inside it, so TERM takes I

blocks.note: what has the buzz is in, fashionable
the i is a British newspaper

annotation.surface: A trendy piece of jargon that has briefly made it into print.
annotation.walkthrough: "Buzz word" reads as a single phrase for jargon, but it splits into two separate words. The i is a British daily paper, a regular crossword source of I.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an interim measure holds only until something permanent replaces it.

entries.clue: Sacred work put on the canvas by painter before noon (5)

indicators.note: places RA ahead of N in the answer

blocks.note: in boxing a knockout puts a fighter on the canvas floor of the ring
N is the abbreviation for noon

annotation.surface: An artist finishing a religious painting before lunchtime.
annotation.walkthrough: With "painter" nearby, "canvas" suggests a picture; it is the floor of a boxing ring.
annotation.definitionFit: The Koran, Islam's holy scripture, is a sacred work in the literal sense of a book held holy.

entries.clue: Nobody airs unimpressive spectacle (3-5)

blocks.note: to vent a view is to air it

annotation.surface: A show so dull that nobody bothers talking about it.
annotation.walkthrough: "Airs" is a verb here, as in airing a grievance.
annotation.definitionFit: A non-event is an occasion that turns out far less impressive than billed.

entries.clue: Going around airport after vacation, drop case (6)

indicators.note: DIVE goes around AT, holding it inside
a vacated word has been emptied, leaving only its first and last letters

blocks.note: to dive is to drop sharply
AIRPORT emptied of its middle leaves A…T

annotation.surface: A traveller home from holiday, going round the airport and dumping a suitcase.
annotation.walkthrough: "Case" reads as luggage but is the grammatical case; "vacation" is not a holiday but the emptying of a word.
annotation.definitionFit: The dative is a grammatical case, marking the indirect object.

entries.clue: Dull, arid hedges are running wild (6)

indicators.note: a hedge surrounds a field, so DRY surrounds the letters
letters running wild are scrambled

annotation.surface: A bleak landscape of parched hedgerows grown out of control.
annotation.walkthrough: "Hedges" looks like a noun in the scenery; it is the verb, to hem in.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something dreary is gloomy and lacking any interest.

entries.clue: Leading journalist expelling Democrat — one working with Bush? (9)

indicators.note: to expel is to throw someone out, so DIARIST throws out its D and loses it

annotation.surface: A senior reporter, not a Democrat, who works alongside President Bush.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital B makes Bush a president; the question mark allows it to be a shrub. A journalist here is someone who keeps a journal, not a reporter.
annotation.definitionFit: A topiarist clips bushes into ornamental shapes.

entries.clue: Funds for journey through Thailand’s capital roughly supporting one (7)

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its first letter
in a down clue, CA sits beneath I and holds it up

annotation.surface: Travel money for a trip through Bangkok, roughly enough for one person.
annotation.walkthrough: "Capital" invites Bangkok; it means the first letter. Viatica is the Latin plural of viaticum.
annotation.definitionFit: A viaticum is an allowance for travelling expenses; viatica is its plural.

entries.clue: Abroad, you back energy-filled dance music, it’s said (9)

indicators.note: 'you back' reads as a verb, but back here means going backwards, so TU is read in reverse
something energy-filled has energy put inside it, so TRANCE is filled with E

blocks.note: trance is a style of electronic dance music

annotation.surface: Overseas, you are praised for backing lively, high-energy dance tracks.
annotation.walkthrough: "Abroad" signals a foreign word: French tu. "You back" reads as supporting someone, but it is the reversal.
annotation.definitionFit: The definition describes rather than names: an utterance is anything spoken aloud, hence 'it's said'.

entries.clue: Way to pen line for poet (5)

indicators.note: to pen an animal is to shut it in, so PATH encloses L

annotation.surface: Advice on how to write a line of verse for a poet.
annotation.walkthrough: "Pen" suggests writing, which suits a poet, but it means enclose.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Sylvia Plath, the American author of Ariel, is one poet among many.

entries.clue: Banker had to move and go for a spin on the road (9,4)

indicators.note: the letters of BANKER HAD are moved around

blocks.note: a go = a turn, as in 'your go'

annotation.surface: A banker forced to relocate, then taking a car out for a drive.
annotation.walkthrough: "Go" is a noun, a turn in a game. A handbrake turn is a skid-turn made by yanking the handbrake while driving.
annotation.definitionFit: A handbrake turn deliberately spins the car round on the road.

entries.clue: Warning partners in game to suppress fury (5)

indicators.note: S and N hold IRE down between them

blocks.note: South and North are partners in bridge

annotation.surface: A caution to a pair of card players to keep their tempers in check.
annotation.walkthrough: In bridge, North and South play as a pair against East and West, so partners can be SN or NS (or EW, WE).
annotation.definitionFit: A siren is an alarm that gives warning, used here as a noun.

entries.clue: What may follow theme song, with note playing after verse (9)

indicators.note: ARIA, TI and ON come after V

blocks.note: an aria is an operatic song
ti (te) is a note of the sol-fa scale
a show that is playing is on

annotation.surface: Musical instructions: after the theme tune comes a note played after a verse.
annotation.walkthrough: "Theme song" reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at theme; song is ARIA.
annotation.definitionFit: In 'theme and variations', each variation follows and alters the theme.

entries.clue: Evidence that insect has drunk alcohol, or giraffe? (8)

blocks.note: surface padding: the words that follow describe a scene, and that description is spelt out literally
what a creature has drunk is in it

annotation.surface: A mock-serious question: what would prove an insect had been drinking, or a giraffe?
annotation.walkthrough: The evidence is simply a description, RUM IN ANT, read as one word.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the giraffe chews the cud like cows and sheep, so it is one of that group.

entries.clue: Strong current answer probing what the wicked get? I’m not sure (9)

indicators.note: A probes into NO REST, sitting inside it

blocks.note: the saying goes 'no rest for the wicked'
er is the hesitant noise of someone unsure

annotation.surface: A doubtful quiz answer about what the sinful receive, backed by a strong current.
annotation.walkthrough: The current is of air, not water: a nor'easter is a strong wind from the northeast.
annotation.definitionFit: A nor'easter is a strong north-easterly wind, a current of air.

entries.clue: Rolls maybe wrapped in protective cover, something baker may use (6)

indicators.note: CAR is wrapped inside BIB

blocks.note: a bib protects clothing while eating

annotation.surface: Bread rolls kept under a cloth in the bakery.
annotation.walkthrough: In a baking scene "Rolls" is bread; the capital R hints at Rolls-Royce.
annotation.definitionFit: Bicarb, bicarbonate of soda, is a raising agent bakers use.

entries.clue: Family member bags diced sage in medicinal powder (8)

indicators.note: to bag is to put in a bag, so MA holds the letters
diced food is chopped up, so the letters are mixed

annotation.surface: Mum stuffs chopped herbs into a home remedy.
annotation.walkthrough: "In" looks like the link to the definition but belongs to the fodder; the definition is just "medicinal powder".
annotation.definitionFit: Magnesia, magnesium oxide, is a white powder taken as an antacid and laxative.

entries.clue: Blackmail, say, is wrong no longer? (6)

blocks.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

annotation.surface: A question whether blackmail has stopped being a crime.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is by example, flagged by "say": blackmail is one way to extort. A tort is the legal term for a civil wrong.
annotation.definitionFit: To extort is to obtain by threats, of which blackmail is an example.

entries.clue: Are witnesses providing snappy dresses? (7)

definitions.note: the definition is a plural verb phrase, matched by the verb 'testify' with a plural subject

indicators.note: to dress is to clothe, so TESTY wraps around IF

annotation.surface: A question about whether witnesses are turning up in smart clothes.
annotation.walkthrough: "Snappy dresses" suggests smart outfits; snappy means irritable, and dresses is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Witnesses testify: 'they testify' can replace 'they are witnesses' in court.

entries.clue: Possible cause of complaint from European bitten by tailless camel (8)

indicators.note: E sits inside the camel's jaws
BACTRIAN loses its final letter

blocks.note: a Bactrian is the two-humped camel; without its last letter

annotation.surface: A tourist complains after being bitten by a camel with no tail.
annotation.walkthrough: "Complaint" means an illness here, not a grievance.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example, using 'complaint' in its sense of illness: germs are one possible cause.

entries.clue: Dismiss article in Bild about king, say (3-4)

indicators.note: about means turned round, as in 'about turn', so DER faces the other way

blocks.note: der is the German for 'the'; Bild is a German newspaper
a king is an example of a playing card

annotation.surface: A German tabloid runs a story about a king being sacked.
annotation.walkthrough: "Article" is not a newspaper story but a grammatical article; the German paper tells you which language.
annotation.definitionFit: A referee red-cards a player to dismiss him from the field.

entries.clue: What happens before the weekend starts to exclude right fans (6)

indicators.note: the R is left out of FRI ENDS

blocks.clueFragment: What happens before the weekend starts
blocks.note: FRI ENDS: Friday ends, then the weekend starts

annotation.surface: Something that happens on Friday afternoons that shuts out right-wing supporters.
annotation.walkthrough: "Starts" belongs to the phrase, not an instruction to take first letters: Friday ends before the weekend starts.
annotation.definitionFit: A fitness fiend or a football fiend is an enthusiast, a fan.

entries.clue: Regular servings of grub with rank taste (9)

indicators.note: regular portions of a word are every other letter

blocks.note: rank = station, one's position in society

annotation.surface: A diner complaining that the food served every day tastes foul.
annotation.walkthrough: "Rank" pairs with "taste" to suggest foul flavour; it means social position, STATION.
annotation.definitionFit: Gustation is the formal word for the act or sense of tasting.

entries.clue: Fat gastronome spilling guts after end of meal (5)

indicators.note: GASTRONOME loses its insides, leaving G…E
after means following in order, so GE is placed behind PUD

blocks.note: pud = pudding, the dessert course that ends a meal

annotation.surface: An overweight foodie overeats until he bursts at the end of dinner.
annotation.walkthrough: "End of meal" looks like the final letter L; it is the pudding, British slang pud.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, though informal: it means podginess, a bit of surplus flab.

entries.clue: Pair of Greek characters in religious artwork (5)

annotation.surface: Two Greek figures depicted in a church painting.
annotation.walkthrough: "Characters" suggests figures in the picture; they are letters of the alphabet.
annotation.definitionFit: A pietà shows the Virgin Mary mourning over the body of Christ.

entries.clue: Son, boring buffoon, shows surprising development (5)

indicators.note: S bores into TWIT, ending up inside

annotation.surface: A dull, foolish son surprises everyone by growing up.
annotation.walkthrough: "Boring" reads as dull; it means drilling into.
annotation.definitionFit: In storytelling this is the plot turn the reader never saw coming.

entries.clue: Fluctuation of fortune, as seen in iconic picture (9)

indicators.note: letters that fluctuate shift about

annotation.surface: A remark that the ups and downs of fortune can be seen in a famous image.
annotation.walkthrough: "Picture" means a film, not a painting: Nosferatu is the 1922 silent vampire film.
annotation.definitionFit: Nosferatu (1922) is an iconic silent film, and a film is a picture.

entries.clue: Powerful Persian seizing power in country (6)

indicators.note: CYRUS grabs P and holds it

blocks.note: Cyrus the Great, founder of the Persian Empire

annotation.surface: A mighty Persian ruler grabbing power in a foreign land.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface fits Cyrus, who really did seize power; here he simply swallows a P.
annotation.definitionFit: Cyprus is an island country in the eastern Mediterranean.

entries.clue: Oasis perhaps with boundless pond by area in desert (7)

indicators.note: POND loses its bounds, its outer letters, leaving ON
A stands beside the rest, at the front

blocks.note: Oasis was a British rock band

annotation.surface: An oasis with a shrunken pond somewhere in the desert.
annotation.walkthrough: In a desert scene, Oasis looks like a water hole; it is the 1990s British band. "Desert" is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Desert' is a verb here, a plain synonym: to leave someone in the lurch.
